strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: proposal.apply can execute a bounded multi-file create_file transaction under Rust-owned permission and apply authority.
The transaction path reuses runtime WriteWorkspace authorization, approved proposal checks, preflight validation, protected path denial, and no-overwrite atomic create semantics.
Apply results record bounded transaction and per-item evidence without raw file content, raw diffs, command output, environment, secrets, or absolute paths.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances controlled_workspace_tools with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement and persistent_structured_ledger behavior.
answers.new_capability: A headless caller can submit one proposal.apply request that creates two to five approved absent files as a bounded transaction.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M6.2 only creates one file per apply; M14 transactions only replace existing files and reject create_file proposals.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie cannot safely materialize a coherent multi-file generated artifact without issuing separate create applies that can partially diverge without transaction evidence.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M22.2 routed headless completion evidence, M22.1 added direct task-run completion evidence, and M21.1 revalidated mode-pack policy for provider retries.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends the existing proposal.apply transaction_items path.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. This extends existing apply result and transaction item evidence rather than adding a report, digest, history, readiness, preview, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime admits homogeneous create_file transactions, verifies current target absence, prepares temporary sibling files, atomically creates targets without overwrite, verifies post-write SHA-256, and records bounded per-item results.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless development can safely create related files in one runtime-owned mutation boundary and decide recovery from bounded transaction evidence.
answers.milestone_progress: This is the first M23 vertical slice and establishes controlled multi-file creation apply execution.

review_value_gate.review_intent: M23.1 must be reviewed for actual bounded multi-file create_file mutation behavior, no-overwrite safety, permission gates, and bounded transaction evidence.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M23.1 changes the current phase manifest only; guard engine changes are not expected.

exit_criteria: proposal.apply accepts two to five homogeneous create_file transaction items using the existing transaction_items request path

Every create_file transaction item requires current approved unconsumed proposal evidence, expected_target_absent=true, latest preflight absence, safe workspace-relative path validation, existing parent directory validation, and symlink rejection
The runtime prepares temporary sibling files before committing target creates and uses no-overwrite atomic creation
A target race or existing target denial leaves other absent targets unwritten and does not consume authorization
Successful transactions record bounded top-level and per-item create evidence with post-write SHA-256 values and no raw file content
Existing single-file create apply and replace transaction apply behavior remain compatible
No new RPC, report, history, digest, readiness, preview, or inspection wrapper is introduced

tests: creates a proposal.apply create_file transaction request

next_phase_candidate_notes: If M23.1 merges, the next M23 phase should add bounded create-file transaction recovery or close M23 if review confirms recovery can rely on existing transaction evidence without a new runtime capability.
